newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 2.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - June 2.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

The Federal Government's decision to cap payments of the A$800 million diesel fuel rebate to mining companies has angered the industry. The decision to limit the rebate revokes an earlier agreement the industry believed had been reached with the Government, in which it accepted tougher eligibility rules for the tax rebate. Page 1

Macquarie Bank, Australia's only home-grown, privately owned investment bank will today announce its first full-year result as a listed company. The company's success has aroused strong interest in both financial and government circles. Page 1.

Members of the Michell family which controls the A$400 million Michell & Sons wool-processing empire have agreed to a A$150 million share buyback as part of a compromise deal that prevents a break-up of the 127-year-old family company. The deal will see two of the four family factions selling their interest to other family members, including company chairman Raymond Michell and managing director John Michell. Page 21

In a reversal of its earlier decision Coca-Cola Amatil Ltd will allow its new shareholder, San Miguel Corporation, to assume a fourth board seat. The move is aimed at appeasing Philippines Government concerns about the A$3.4 billion stock and asset swap between the two companies. Page 21.

Australis Media Ltd is to consider leasing its satellite assets to Optus Vision. The move is a response to the New South Wales Supreme Court's ruling against the A$25 million satellite infrastructure sharing deal that had been worked out between the two companies. Page 21.

Perpetual Trustees Australia Ltd chairman John Lamble believes there should be more exchange of information between companies and individual shareholders. In support of this he recently wrote to his company's shareholders predicting a 20 per cent profit increase for the year to June 30, and increases in the final dividend. Page 22.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The ANZ Bank is likely to consider an outsider to replace chief executive Don Mercer. While the company has several suitable internal candidates, the industry believes that none have the mixture of youth and expertise which the position requires. Page 29

Australis chief executive Sean O'Halloran has rejected calls for a rationalisation of the pay TV industry. O'Halloran did not rule out the prospect of Australis merging with a competitor, citing the increased access to capital such a move would bring. Page 29

Hopes of a further easing of monetary policy by the Reserve Bank have been fuelled by reports of slow national growth rates for the March quarter. Colonial State Bank chief economist Hans Kunnen has predicted a March quarter GDP growth rate of 0.5 per cent, and an annual economic growth rate of 1.9 per cent. Page 29

Shell and British Petroleum have allied themselves with environmentalists in conceding that oil companies must recognise the threat posed by industry-induced climate change and move to renewable energy sources. The admission represents a break from the global oil industry's prevalent position. Page 29

The owner of Adelaide-based medical company Dynek, Patricia Crook, claims export revenue from health services and medical equipment could rival the education industry's A$2 billion a year, but it is being hampered by the negative attitude of the Australian medical profession towards local products. Dynek is a producer of medical sutures and a successful exporter. Page 30 --

Investors in managed funds and unit trusts may soon be able to discard trustees as supervisors of investments under proposals now being discussed in the collective investments industry. The trustee industry is said to be close to an agreement which would allow trust-free investment products offered alongside the existing system. Page 31.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Network Entertainment has had a disappointing performance since it listed on the stock exchange last December. Setbacks have included loss of important contracts, unexpected reductions in profit figures and the recent departure of chairman John Hewson. Pge 37.

Brierley Investments is expected to seek to buy Westpac's three per cent stake in John Fairfax Holdings, when restrictions on its current 19.99 per cent sharehold level are removed in two weeks. A spokesman for Westpac said the shares were not considered strategic holdings but merely part of the bank's in-house principal trading operation. Page 37.

The Australian Taxation Office is preparing for a crackdown to coincide with the new financial year, on the two problematical areas of the cash economy and international profit sharing. A report on the cash economy, prepared by the ATO's cash economy task force, is to be released this week. Page 37.

The Wool Council of Australia is set to introduce far-reaching reforms designed to modernise the wool industry. The Council hopes the reforms will restore its dwindling stocks with growers, and distance it from the Federal Government. Page 37.

West Australian based grocery wholesaler Foodland Associated has attracted increased industry interest following its recent profit upgrades resulting from the improved earnings outlook of its New Zealand operations. The company's share price has risen to A$8.40, with a revised net profit of A$55 million now being predicted. Page 40.

-- James Hardie Industries will this Thursday release a full-year profit result that is expected to calm shareholder fears and encourage hopes for the company's future growth. Analysts predict James Hardie will post a net profit of approximately A$50 million, turning around a recent string of disappointing results. Page 40.
THE AGE

A Reuters survey of 28 financial institutions has found that most market economists have predicted Australia's official growth rate will fall to between 2 and 2.5 per cent after the release of the March-quarter national accounts on Wednesday. Most of those surveyed believe the figures will show growth of between 0.5 and 1 per cent for the quarter. Page B1.

Brierly Investments Ltd may seek to buy a three per cent share in John Fairfax Holdings that is currently owned by Westpac subsidiary the Immunised Share Trading Account. The Westpac share of 22.75 million Fairfax shares could be bought out by BIL when it is allowed to raise its shareholding in Fairfax above its present level of 19.9 per cent. Page B1.

Network Entertainment has found life as a listed company difficult. The company is now valued at less than A$5 million after being valued at A$34 million six months ago, and has lost key figures from its management, including chairman and former Federal opposition Leader Dr John Hewson. Page B1.

Melbourne-based company Celebrity Wigs general manager Paul Shiff says the company places heavy emphasis on making modern hairpieces unnoticeable. Shiff inherited his family company from his parents and has expanded it so that he now employs 14 people on the factory floor, and has stores in both Chapel Street in Melbourne and Oxford Street in Sydney. Page B3.

A survey by Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu of over 1400 chief information officers in 21 countries reveals that while over 95 per cent of them expect electronic commerce to increase, the companies they represent are still reluctant to fully integrate the electronic age into their business. An accompanying European survey found 80 per cent of consumers said they would use smart cards for security. Page B2.

Federal Government funding has been withdrawn from the First Place small business information centres. Vic Small Business Minister Louise Asher announced recently the scheme clashed with Federal plans to outsource employment services, but sources also claim that conflict within First Place was a factor in the decision. Page B3
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom, 61-2 9373-1800
